items.normalized_sql:
SELECT o.customer_id, c.customer_name, sum(o.total_amount) AS total_amount
FROM orders o
INNER JOIN customers c
ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.status = 'APPROVED'
AND o.customer_id IN (
SELECT customer_id
FROM customer_segments
WHERE segment_code = 'VIP' )
GROUP BY o.customer_id, c.customer_name
HAVING sum(o.total_amount) > 1000

patterns.description: Uses explicit INNER JOIN clauses with ON predicates to connect source tables.
Applies AND-connected row filters in WHERE and relies on IN-based predicates.
evidence: WHERE o.status = 'APPROVED' AND o.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM customer_segments WHERE segment_code = 'VIP')

patterns.description: Uses nested SELECT subqueries as part of the filtering logic.
Groups aggregated rows by o.customer_id, c.customer_name. Applies a HAVING filter after aggregation.
